bat.root_cause: Three-layer problem: (1) cargo not in PATH (/usr/local/cargo/bin/cargo exists but not in shell PATH — command -v cargo returns empty). (2) Compile.sh unconditionally overwrites ./executable with wrapper to /usr/local/bin/bat. (3) /usr/local/bin/bat does NOT exist in Hetzner eval container (confirmed). Result: returncode 127 on all binary invocations. The 66 passing tests are those that test error conditions (returncode != 0). The staging eval (2286/2664) used a LOCAL Docker image that had /usr/local/bin/bat cached from a prior run — not reproducible on Hetzner. Workspace: github.com/astaxie/bat (Go HTTP client) NOT sharkdp/bat (Rust syntax highlighter). Tests test sharkdp/bat syntax-highlighting behavior, so building Go source would also fail behavior tests.
bat.next_action: DRIVER_HOLD. Fix path: (1) add export PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:$PATH to compile.sh. (2) Include sharkdp/bat Rust source in tarball (from sharkdp/bat GitHub). (3) Build with cargo build --release -- output to /usr/local/bin/bat. (4) Remove unconditional wrapper overwrite — only create wrapper after binary installed. Estimated 178+ hours of work. Alternatively: write Python/shell wrapper implementing bat's syntax-highlighting API surface.
